chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who gave something to his son, [asking]: Is it permissible for him to take it back?
He (peace be upon him) said: "Yes, unless he is a child."

key_terms.نُحْلِ: Gifting (voluntary transfer of property without compensation)
key_terms.هِبَةٍ: Gift (synonymous with nahl in this context)
key_terms.يَرْجِعَ فِيهِ: To revoke or take back the gift

ai.seo_question: Can a father take back a gift he gave to his son in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that revocation of a gift (nahl) is generally permissible, but introduces a specific exception for young children, reflecting the juristic principle that gifts to minors are often considered irrevocable to protect their interests. This ruling highlights the nuanced approach in Shia fiqh regarding the finality of gifts based on the recipient's capacity, distinguishing it from general contractual revocations. The hadith underscores the importance of intent and the recipient's status in determining the legal permanence of the transfer.
